key_insight: Individualized Bayesian tuning of a classical Biquad Filter-Burg model matched or outperformed neural and classical EEG phase estimators with substantially less calibration time.
engineering_relevance: BOB offers a calibration-efficient approach to real-time EEG phase estimation for closed-loop neuromodulation, including stimulus-aligned theta activity.
method: Characterize spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering.
Use Bayesian optimization to individualize the Biquad Filter-Burg phase estimator.
Benchmark against DBCNN, EPN, Phastimate, and PEAP under matched testing conditions.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used stimulation-evoked theta EEG from 20 healthy subjects and resting-state alpha EEG from 20 LEMON participants, with matched channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation times, and an offline zero-phase-filter/Hilbert reference.
watch_item: Results in healthy-subject recordings do not establish performance in clinical populations or deployed closed-loop systems.
paper_title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
